subject: OKR stability playbook — re-scope proposal & dependency asks
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: OKR stability playbook — re-scope proposal & dependency asks

Team —

Quick status: the core stability OKR (Reduce 95th pct inference latency by 15%) is tracking at ~9% improvement on our staged traffic after the last patch, but test variance and a couple of infra constraints mean we will likely miss the target if we keep the current rollout plan. I pulled together a short playbook (attached) with a proposed re-scope and a prioritized dependency list for the next two weeks. Highlights: 

- Proposal: shift the target to 12% for Q3 internal commitment and run a focused P1 initiative to recover the remaining 3% in Q3->Q4. This preserves reliability for customers while giving us runway for kernel-level optimizations.
- Blockers: need dedicated infra slots for distributed load tests (3x GPUs for 48h), a product canary sign-off window aligned with the Ded cluster, and a legal review for the proposed SLA wording if we change the public commitment.
- Risks: if we delay, downstream billing and SLO reporting for two sets of high-traffic customers will show a regression.

Ask: Please review the attached deck and confirm the dependency owners below or suggest alternates. If we can lock owners and dates by EOD Wed (Jul 28), I’ll push the QBR slide set to exec and vendor partners.

Dependency grid (proposed owners):
- Infra: Acme platform team — request: dedicated 3-GPU slot for e2e load test (Owner: acme-platform-eng@acme.com)
- Product/Canary: Naomi — request: 24h canary on Ded cluster during week of Aug 2
- Kernel/Perf: Markus — request: toggle quantization + kernel A/B and run perf bench by Jul 30
- Legal/SLA: Laura — request: 48h review of revised SLA blurb (I’ll attach suggested copy)
- CS/Customer comms: Marissa — request: draft comms and rollback playbook

Attachments: 2026-07-26-okr-stability-deck.pdf (3 slides + appendix), runbook_qbr_notes.md

Next steps I’ll take after owners confirmed: update QBR slide (exec summary + risk table), open infra ticket with Acme, and schedule a Monday sync (Aug 2) to confirm canary window.

Thanks — Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Director, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR stability playbook — re-scope proposal & dependency asks

Diego — thanks for the write-up and deck. Quick thoughts:

1) I agree with a conservative public commit (12%) and then an aggressive engineering track for the remaining delta. We should call this out explicitly in the QBR as a mitigation strategy so Sales/CS don't over-promise.
2) I can take the canary sign-off but need Marissa to confirm we have a rollback hook tested (canary must be safe to revert in <30 minutes). Markus — can you confirm your kernel toggle has a clean fallback?
3) Timeline question: if infra can only provide slots the week of Aug 9, we'll need a plan B (run per-node benches locally and synthetic traffic in parallel).

I’ll carve time Tues morning to draft the canary acceptance criteria and will post to the Drive link.

Naomi

To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR stability playbook — re-scope proposal & dependency asks

Diego / team —

I can own the kernel/perf work. Two quick technical clarifications: 

- The 9% improvement you measured — was that with mixed-precision only or with the new attention kernel enabled? If it's mixed-precision only, we should expect an extra 1–2% from the attention kernel on long sequences.
- For toggles: I’ll produce a canary image that supports both kernels and a clear flag to switch back. I’ll aim to have perf benches by Jul 30 and a canary image by Aug 1.

If infra can’t give us distributed slots in time, I’ll coordinate with Marissa to run the same bench set on the Ded cluster with a reduced shard layout; results will be comparable for decisioning.

Markus

Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR stability playbook — re-scope proposal & dependency asks

Diego / team —

I’ll own CS/customer comms and the rollback playbook. Quick notes:

- Rollback: we have an established flow for Ded canaries; I’ll validate the <30m rollback end-to-end with SRE and post the test checklist by Wed EOD.
- Infra slots: I pinged Acme (cc’d) for availability; earliest they offered is Aug 9–10. If we can’t get an earlier slot, plan B is to run per-node benches + synthetic traffic; we should still hit a decision threshold for QBR.
- Customer messaging: recommend we lead with operational stability improvements and the measured 9% benefit, then call out the plan to reach 12% public and 15% longer-term; avoids sounding like a rollback.

Attachment: runbook_qbr_notes.md (draft)

Marissa

Thanks, all.

Laura here — I can run a 48-hour legal review on the revised SLA blurb; please include the suggested blurb in the Drive doc and I’ll prioritize it.

Decision points for QBR slide:
- Confirm public commit (12%) — Diego: please send the exact wording you want on the slide.
- Confirm infra plan (Plan A: Aug 2 canary with Acme; Plan B: per-node benches + synthetic if slots delayed) — Marissa, please confirm rollback checklist by Wed EOD.
- Exec ask: sign-off on the re-scope and permission to communicate the mitigation plan to Sales.

I’ll block 30 minutes Thu to review the slide and the SLA blurb with Diego.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Policy
Redwood Inference
